seo.description: The bathroom brands we fit in Twyford, and how our fit-only installation model works — your products, our labour, from period-style Lefroy Brooks to contemporary Crosswater and Laufen.

h1: Bathroom brands we fit in Twyford

hero.intro: We work on a fit-only basis across Twyford, which means we install the bathroom products you've already chosen — from a showroom, a designer's specification, or your own research — rather than selling you a fixed catalogue of our own. Twyford's split housing profile makes this especially relevant: the village grew up along the railway line between Reading and Maidenhead, leaving an older centre of period cottages and terraces surrounded by commuter-belt housing added in later waves, and the brassware and sanitaryware that suit a compact, older cottage bathroom are a genuinely different fitting job to the fittings that suit a larger, more recently built house with room to spare. Across the projects we work on in and around Twyford, a recurring set of brands turns up again and again, spanning both ends of that period-to-contemporary spread.

sections.heading: The fit-only model, explained
sections.body: Fit-only means exactly what it says: the labour and installation expertise, without us also supplying or marking up the products. You choose your sanitaryware, brassware and tiles through whichever route suits you — a bathroom showroom, an online retailer, a designer's specification, or a brand's own stockist — and we fit them properly. This matters in Twyford because of how much the specification can vary within a small village: a period cottage in the older centre might call for traditional exposed pipework and cross-head handles sized sensibly for a narrower room, while a newer commuter-belt house further out is more likely to be specified with concealed, minimal brassware and a larger walk-in shower. Either way, the quote you get reflects labour and fitting complexity honestly, rather than bundling in a retail margin on the products themselves, and we confirm exactly what's been specified before a wall closes up or a screen goes in.

sections.heading: Brands we fit
sections.body: For the traditional end of what we fit in Twyford, Lefroy Brooks and Burlington come up regularly in the period cottages and terraces of the older village centre, where a narrower room and a period aesthetic often go together. Lefroy Brooks is built around exposed pipework, cross-head handles and period-inspired profiles rather than concealed, minimal fittings, which means the pipe runs, brackets and wall fixings have to be set out and finished to be looked at, not hidden — every joint is visible once the room is done, and that's a particular discipline in a compact cottage bathroom where there's less wall space to route pipework discreetly. Burlington reproduces classic forms — pedestal and wall-hung basins, close-coupled and high-level WCs, roll-top baths — with a modern fixing standard underneath the traditional silhouette, so getting the period look right depends on fixing choices such as a high-level cistern bracket or a wall-hung basin's hidden support that aren't visible once the room is finished. At the more contemporary end, which tends to suit the larger, more recently built commuter-belt houses further from the centre, Crosswater's concealed valves and minimal deck-mounted taps are designed to disappear into the wall or worktop, which means the wall build-up and pipework depth have to be right well before the tiler arrives, and Laufen's SaphirKeramik basins and pans have noticeably finer rims and sharper geometry than standard vitreous china, which makes handling and sequencing on site a bigger consideration than with a heavier, more conventional basin. Geberit concealed cisterns and wall-hung WCs, and hansgrohe and GROHE brassware, come up across both ends of that spread in Twyford, because correct frame selection and fixing, and knowing exactly which valve or mixer has been specified, matter whatever the age or style of the room. For baths, Kaldewei's titanium-enamelled steel needs even, accurate bearing across the full base rather than the flex-prevention an acrylic support relies on, and Villeroy & Boch sanitaryware and baths turn up regularly too — precise ceramics with hard-wearing glaze finishes, where the detail that matters most is matching the flush plate, pan and frame generations correctly before anything is ordered.

sections.heading: Why the right brand detail matters across Twyford's mix of old and new
sections.body: Because Twyford genuinely spans a compact period village centre and a spread of newer commuter-belt housing, getting the fitting detail right isn't just about the brand — it's about matching the installation approach to the property and the room it's going into. A period cottage with a narrower bathroom and exposed pipework needs brackets and pipe runs set out to be looked at within a tighter space, not boxed away, while a newer commuter-belt house with concealed brassware needs the wall build-up and pipework depth right before the tiler arrives, because none of that is visible once the room is finished and it's expensive to correct afterwards. We work through exactly what's been specified at survey, confirm the installation route for whichever brand and era of fitting is involved, and sequence the job so the product — whether it's a style built to echo the period the cottage actually dates from, or a thoroughly contemporary fitting going into a newer build — ends up installed the way it's designed to be.

faqs.q: Do I have to buy my bathroom products from you?
faqs.a: No. We work fit-only, which means you choose and supply your own sanitaryware, brassware and tiles — through a showroom, designer or retailer — and we handle the installation to the standard those products need.

faqs.q: Which bathroom brands do you fit most often in Twyford?
faqs.a: Lefroy Brooks and Burlington come up regularly in Twyford's period cottages and terraces in the older village centre, where a narrower room and a period style are often specified together. Geberit, hansgrohe and GROHE turn up across all of Twyford's housing types, and Crosswater and Laufen are more common in the larger, newer commuter-belt houses further out.

faqs.q: Do Twyford's period cottages need different brands to its newer commuter-belt houses?
faqs.a: Not necessarily different brands, but often a different style and scale within them — exposed pipework and traditional cross-head taps sized for a narrower room suit a period cottage in the village centre, while concealed, minimal brassware and larger walk-in showers are more typical in a newer commuter-belt house. We confirm what's been specified at survey and fit accordingly.

faqs.q: Can you fit a brand that isn't listed here?
faqs.a: In most cases, yes — we work through the specific installation requirements of whatever's been specified at survey stage. If a product has an unusual fixing or frame requirement, we confirm it before anything is ordered rather than discovering it on fitting day.

faqs.q: Do you work with Twyford bathroom showrooms and designers?
faqs.a: Yes. A lot of the specification we fit in Twyford has already been through a showroom consultation or designer before we're brought in at survey stage, and we're used to working from an existing specification rather than starting from scratch.

image.heroPrompt: Purpose: hero image for the Twyford brands-in-area page, implying brand and material choice through a close-to-mid fixture detail rather than a full room shot. Subject and action: a concealed, minimal deck-mounted basin mixer tap mounted above a floating oak-fronted vanity unit, positioned as if mid-way through a showroom specification decision, no water running. Setting and work-stage: a finished bathroom vanity wall inside a newer commuter-belt house on the edge of Twyford, daytime, bright directional daylight entering from an unseen side window. Composition: close-to-fixture mid shot centred on the tap and basin, oak vanity top filling the lower third of the frame, softly out-of-focus tiled wall in the background. Light and materials: warm oak vanity cabinetry, brushed brass deck-mounted tap, bright directional daylight raking across the brass fitting at a shallow angle creating uneven highlight and shadow rather than flat light. Constraints: no people, no text, no logos, no brand names visible on any fixture, no LED lighting strips anywhere in frame, no symmetrical twin-basin staging, no uniform gold or amber colour wash, no hanging plants, florals or candles, no water shown running from the tap, brushed brass fitting should show faint, believable handling marks rather than uniform showroom-new gloss.
